steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook elbow macaroni in the boiling water, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes; drain.
Place a saucepan over medium-low heat; add cheese , milk, and black pepper. Cook until cheese has melted, stirring frequently. Stir in drained macaroni until evenly coated.

raw_recipe.headline: Easiest Mac-N-Cheese Ever!
raw_recipe.description: Make homemade macaroni and cheese with elbow macaroni, cubed processed cheese, milk, and black pepper. This is the easiest mac-n-cheese recipe ever.
raw_recipe.name: Easiest Mac-N-Cheese Ever!

review.reviewBody: This is so easy and my kids can even make this own their own. If you use whole wheat pasta it gives it more texture, which is better, and 1/2 the processed cheese and 1/2 shredded whatever you like tastes great!!! Excellent recipe.

I am giving this a four because I don't think the serving size was correct. I had to add a lot more processed cheese to make it not so dry. My dad, the homemade mac and cheese lover seemed to like it, and the kids loved it.

I used a can of evaporated milk, one 4oz. cube of velveeta cut into pieces, 1.5 cups of shredded mexican blend cheese. heated the milk to a simmer, added the cheeses until sauce became smooth an velvety. added onion powder, garlic powder, lawry's season salt, black pepper and dry mustard. Also used cavatappi pasta, its what I had on hand. Yummy!!! 
leftovers were solid, but put in a saucepan with a 1/4 cup of milk to re-heat and was the same as the day I made it. Yummy!!!

Great recipe but tmake it even EASIER put cheese and milk through processor no need to heat on stove forever. Mix in a dish and put in oven for 20-30 min.also I changed it to make an awesome adult dish. Using 8oz. of cheese and 1 pound of macaroni I added a can of Rottel tomatoes & green chiles ( comes in mild, medium or hot) 1/4 cup parmesean cheese and I cut up 2 packages of imitation crab. mixed together and bake. You can top with shredded cheddar and/or bread crumbs. super fast. and OMG soooo good.

The few weeks prior to Christmas, especially when I'm traveling, is a time when I welcome fast, easy recipes, but I still want a good meal. Mixing up some Velveeta with cooked noodles is a no-brainer, really, but it was a real inspiration and time-saver for me tonight. Skipping the steps of a roux and/or a period of time in the oven simplified this macaroni and cheese, and in my opinion didn't really compromise it. In all fairness, however, I couldn't resist adding a good blob of butter and a couple tablespoons of Vermont Cheese Powder (King Arthur Flour's). This was so convincing compared to the "real deal" that Hubs didn't even know the difference - and had I not cooked it myself, I'm not sure I would have either. It just goes to show you that a dish being labor intensive doesn't necessarily make it that much better - if at all.
Super easy and worked well for the mac n cheese bar I set up for my son's birthday party. We had toppings like pulled pork, jalapenos, breadcrumbs, and bacon bits! Great base recipe!

The first time, I followed the recipe exactly. 2nd time I grated cheese by hand, as we have trouble going through an entire block of processed cheese - you know what I mean. Today, I used half a jar of Kraft's Old English cheese spread - even easier! Thank you for a terrific recipe - which is great for a smaller family. Perfect for two. Approximately the same quantity as the blue box mac and cheese - you know what I mean there, too.
This is the same recipe that I have been making for years because it is the one on the Velvetta cheese box. I use 2 cups of macaroni and it makes enough for 5 people easily.

I used to work at a pizza place that made this exact recipe minus the pepper and penne was used instead of elbow noodles. You can melt the milk and processed cheese in the microwave. I did however try it at home with 2% processed cheese and low fat milk and have to admit the full fat version with whole milk & regular processed cheese is much yummier. This dish is addicting especially when you realize just how easy it is.

This was a good recipe to finish that cheese in the fridge. I agree with the others that it is a bit bland; but that is why my kids like, so this is a keeper. This would serve as a good base for more ingredients to increase the flavor.

Love this! I took advise of others and added a couple of table spoons of butter and cheddar for a 1/4 of the amount of cheese it called for. I don't think the serving size is accurate though...I double the recipe and it fed 4....I suspected this and that is why I doubled it but thought others might benefit from reading. Definitely will make again, and again! Thank you :)
Add onions, green peppers and cooked Philly cheesesteak and you have Philly Mac.
This was a family favorite when my kids were young. I always added a protein such as hamburger, cubed ham or chicken.

It tastes good but the cheese ended up being clumped up and really hard to chew, so i took some shredded cheese and added it and took out the clumps of the other cheese. Other than that it tasted pretty good
Its awesome!

I don't know about y'all, but I only got 2 servings from this, not 6, but is that because the submitter meant it to be a side not a main dish? I served it as a main, so of course the portion was larger than a side would have been. As far as flavor, it's Velveeta, and pretty much just Velveeta, which makes a thick creamy cheesy sauce. The milk adds no flavor, it simply thins the melted cheese into a sauce. This is much better than anything in a box. Yes, it takes slightly more work than squeezing cheese sauce from a pouch, but it's a few cuts with a knife, and some patience while stirring over heat to melt the cheese. It takes a few minutes, but it's superior to the boxed stuff and doesn't take much longer, and very little effort. This isn't comparable to the mac and cheese with a roux base and lot of cheddar and fancy cheeses, or baked mac and cheese, but it's simple, fast, and hits the spot. Stovetop mac and cheese has it's place too. It's humble and comforting.
My 3 yr old granddaughter loves it 😋
